page: The Amazon Web Services c8ine.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, offering 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is equipped with an extensive 480 MB Level 3 cache, 2 MB Level 2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering a compute-centric 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps, includes zero integrated local storage drives, and features no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2281.0 and text processing workloads at 2984.0. Single-threaded data handling tests, such as gzip compression at 34.44 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.67 GB/sec, fall into the top 25 percent performance bracket. In quantized AI inference, text generation throughput using a 135M parameter model reaches 391.04 tokens per second, aided by onboard AMX instructions. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, stay within the median range relative to its core count.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance maximizes CPU clock speeds and vector capabilities within a compact 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation. Because it contains no bundled local storage, persistent file systems and databases must rely entirely on remote Amazon EBS volumes over network bandwidth. The c8ine.4xlarge is designed for compute-bound operations, including high-throughput static web serving, Clang-based software compilation, single-threaded processing pipelines, and small-model machine learning inference.
description: The Amazon Web Services c8ine.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor utilizing x86_64 architecture under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, it maintains a 2 GB per core ratio along with a large 480 MB L3 cache. Vector processing is reinforced by AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets. The server contains no local storage and lacks discrete GPUs, routing storage I/O and communication over a 25 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core compute, high-throughput text processing, and swift small-model LLM generation. It serves CPU-heavy tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, compression pipelines, and targeted machine learning inference.
